newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts dither before sales data,watch Bunds.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts dither before sales data,watch Bunds.

text.p: UK government bond futures were little changed in early trade as the market awaits the release of key retail sales data due at 0830 GMT and watches an indecisive performance from Bunds.
"We're basically drifting around before the numbers. We're just going to copy Bunds," one gilt salesman at a UK brokerage said.
0708 GMT, LIFFE September gilts were down 1/32 at 114-1/32 whilst September Bunds were down three basis points at 101.29.
UK retail sales data for May are expected to show a monthly increase of 0.2 percent and an annual rise of 4.5 percent, down from 4.7 in April.
"There's been some concern of late that we might see a strong figure but the data have come down of late and it's all a bit more relaxed,' another gilt salesman said.
"But it's really incredibly dull this morning, gilts really aren't in the picture," he said.
The market is on hold before the July 2 budget, in which Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown is expected to deliver a fiscal drain of some 3.0 billion stg.

The minutes of the first, and indeed the final, monthly monetary meeting between Bank of England Governor Eddie George and Chancellor Brown are also due at 0830 GMT but are likely to have little impact given the meeting resulted in a 1/4 point rise in interest rates.

"The shock value may be very limited since in previous meetings the Bank of England had called for a 25 basis point hike in rates and that's what they got,' said Royal Bank of Scotland economist Neil Parker.
Moreover, official interest rates have since been increased by another 1/4 point, taking them to 6.5 percent.
At the short end of the yield curve, there was also little movement with LIFFE September short sterling unmoved at 93.16.
